audit.recode_to: weight-sensitive iambic, feet built left-to-right, no degenerate feet, primary stress on the rightmost complete foot (Souza 2013 sec. 2.4): all-light words second stress 0201 02010 (final in even-parity words, penult in odd-parity words); heavy syllables (Vː or glide coda) foot themselves and take stress (['jãː.tã] vs [jã.'tã]). Cite Souza 2013 pp.70-75 as deciding source; keep Paula 2004 sec. 2.7 and Garcia 2002 sec. 2.6 as 'contra' (Paula: word-final incl. after suffixation; Garcia: root-final, suffixes unstressed) with a caution flag that the three descriptions disagree on trisyllables and on suffixed forms. If the catalog must stay conservative, at minimum downgrade 'fixed-dominant final' to contested and add the two contra entries.

sources.quote: 'o Item Lexical ... tem acento fixo na primeira sílaba da direita para a esquerda, sendo que os afixos não atraem o acento — não modificando assim a acentuação' ... 'o acento proeminente na língua Yawanawá é fixo na base do item lexical (IL) e os afixos não atraem o acento.' Examples: [ʃa'raxu] /ʃara-xu/ 'bom-PL', [a'jatu] /aja-tu/, [ma'nia] /mani-a/, [u'pejnu] /upaj-nu/. I.e. root-final, not word-final: directly contradicts Paula's claim that suffixation moves stress to the word-final syllable.

sources.note: Independent earlier description: stress root-final, affixes do not attract stress ([ʃa'raxu], [a'jatu]) — a second source against word-final fixed stress.

sources.quote: Explicitly quotes and rejects Paula 2004: 'Proponho, porém, que o Yawanawá apresenta um padrão iâmbico de acentuação, com pés moraicos formados da esquerda para a direita, com o acento primário recaindo no primeiro pé completo, da direita para a esquerda.' Even-syllable words are final-stressed ([ma.'pu], [nu.ˌwɨ.ta.'pa]) but trisyllables are NOT: [ka.'ɾa.ta] 'rim', [ka.'ɾã.pa], [na.'ka.ʃɨ], [a.'wĩ.hu] vs [a.ˌwĩ.hu.'hu], [ɨ.'wa.pa] vs [ɨ.ˌwa.pa.'ma]; no degenerate feet; heavy syllables (long V or glide coda) form their own foot and attract stress: ['jãː.tã] 'segurou' vs [jã.'tã] 'tarde', ['iː.
sources.locator: sec. 2.4 Acento, pp.70-75; 2.8 p.~93 (conclusão do capítulo)
sources.note: Most recent and only metrical treatment of Yawanawá stress; explicitly rejects Paula 2004's word-final rule (our deciding source) in favour of weight-sensitive L-to-R iambs with non-final stress in trisyllables — changes the classification.
